source_of_truth: The frozen judge-only reference dossier; candidates answer from internal knowledge.
evaluation_principles: Reward explicit reasoning at failure boundaries.
Require idempotency to represent one stable business intent.
Demand a bounded, realistic guarantee rather than exactly-once magic.

key_facts.label: Ambiguous timeout
key_facts.expected: Explains that a timeout cannot distinguish an unprocessed request from a completed operation whose response was lost.

key_facts.label: Duplicate-after-charge failure
key_facts.expected: Shows how a crash after charging but before durable local completion or acknowledgement can cause a retry and second charge.

key_facts.label: Stable payment idempotency key
key_facts.expected: Scopes one stable key to one logical payment intent and preserves it across retries while preventing mismatched reuse.

key_facts.label: Durable local deduplication
key_facts.expected: Uses inbox, processed-message state or uniqueness plus atomic local transitions rather than an in-memory check.

key_facts.label: Kafka guarantee boundary
key_facts.expected: Limits Kafka exactly-once semantics to supported Kafka transactional flows and excludes automatic atomicity with the provider or arbitrary DB.

key_facts.label: Transactional outbox role
key_facts.expected: Uses an outbox to atomically couple local business state and outgoing events while retaining duplicate-safe publication or consumption.

key_facts.label: State and concurrency
key_facts.expected: Uses explicit payment states, stable identifiers and concurrency or uniqueness controls.

key_facts.label: Reconciliation
key_facts.expected: Uses provider queries, webhooks and reconciliation to resolve unknown or missed states.

key_ideas.label: Exactly once is end-to-end
key_ideas.expected: Evaluates the guarantee across all side-effect boundaries rather than inheriting a broker feature name.

key_ideas.label: Make retries safe
key_ideas.expected: Designs duplicates as expected and renders repeat attempts harmless or detectable.

key_ideas.label: Separate atomicity problems
key_ideas.expected: Distinguishes Kafka transactions, local DB plus event atomicity, and external-provider idempotency.

key_ideas.label: Convergence over impossible certainty
key_ideas.expected: States a bounded safety goal plus eventual reconciliation and observability.

known_critical_errors.description: Claims Kafka exactly-once automatically prevents duplicate calls or charges at an external provider.
Recommends blind retries of a non-idempotent charge after ambiguous timeouts.
Uses a fresh idempotency key for each retry of the same payment intent.
Claims a transactional outbox makes an external charge atomic with a local database transaction.
Omits any reconciliation path for unknown external outcomes.

anchors.25: No material distributed-systems or payment-safety error.
anchors.20: Accurate overall with one minor imprecision.
anchors.12: At least one major error or several meaningful imprecisions.

anchors.10: Uses concrete failure timelines and integrates the controls into a coherent design.
anchors.7: Sound design with one underdeveloped connection.
anchors.4: Lists patterns without tracing failures or boundaries.
anchors.0: Does not explain the reliability problem.

anchors.10: States exact boundaries and realistic safety or convergence guarantees.
anchors.7: Mostly precise with one limited overstatement.

anchors.10: Clear German, descriptive structure and useful to an experienced developer.

anchors.5: High information density without material repetition.
anchors.0: Exceeds the hard maximum or is not focused.
